Switch does the hard part

Eight things only Switch gives this project

The gate holds the merge rules. Switch gives it people, agents and proof of who said what. Pick one to see what breaks without it.

The moment it exists for

A commit lands after the approval

Chat approvals usually mean "this pull request is fine". Here an approval names one commit, and the gate re-reads GitHub before it merges.

Commit under review

Do this yourself in the demo →
Why it's needed

Coding agents write fixes in minutes. Trusting them is the hard part.

One more commit lands after "looks good".

An approval names a full commit. Any new commit voids the evidence.

An agent says its tests passed when they never ran.

The gate trusts GitHub's CI results and a signed report tied to one run and one commit.

A public bug report carries instructions aimed at the agent.

No agent sees a report until a maintainer accepts it, and it arrives fenced as untrusted data.

Your turn

Take one bug from report to merge

You type the same messages a real team types and read the gate's real answers. The evidence console is the real app. The other screens are close copies, labelled as such.

    What each part of Switch does here

    What Switch providesWhat Loopback does with itWithout it

    GitHub is the source of truth for code. Switch is the source of truth for who said what, and where. The button on this page doesn't stop a server, because nothing here is running. It shows what you would see, and the refusal above is the gate's own wording, from starting it with Switch unreachable.

    Implementation

    How it's built

    A Node 22 and TypeScript service connects to Switch as an agent, keeps its state and audit log in SQLite, and is the only identity allowed to merge on GitHub.

    The parts, and where they are

    PartWhat it doesCode

    Real code from the gate

    These excerpts are cut from the source each time this page is built.

    How this page works

    On this pageHow it's made
    Chat replies from the gateRecorded from the gate's real router, permissions, state machine and merge policy (apps/switch-gate/src/demo/rehearsal.ts), which check 16 outcomes as they run.
    Evidence consoleThe real React app from apps/console. It reads responses recorded from the real API in apps/console-api, taken at each step of that run. Its settings panel is filled in from the rehearsal's own settings, because the API doesn't serve them yet.
    TerminalWhat npm run demo printed during that run. Setup commands come from docs/setup.md.
    Team chat layoutRebuilt from a running Mattermost 11.9. It's a copy of the layout, and only the recorded messages get answers.
    Switch Console screensIllustrations unless marked as screenshots. Field labels come from the real template file.
    The Switch buttonSwitches this page to what happens with no Switch: messages aren't delivered, no step can run, and the console shows no case. The refusal text is the gate's real wording, and a test fails if it changes in the code.
    The buildnpm run demo:page (scripts/build-demo-page.mjs). It writes nothing if the rehearsal fails.

    Not proven yet

    • On the live run a person guided the verifier step by step. It hasn't yet completed its brief alone.
    • The agents ran on the host, not in their isolated containers, so verification is labelled advisory in chat. A signature proves a report wasn't altered, not that its tests ran. A person should review the diff before approving.
    • A commit landing after approval hasn't been seen live, nor have why, board, team and the room documents. The rehearsal and tests cover them, against stand-ins for Switch.
    • Nobody else has done the live setup from a clean clone, and the template hasn't been run end to end.

    Run it yourself

    This same rehearsal runs on your machine in about two minutes. You need Node 22 and no accounts.

    git clone https://github.com/puneetnith28/Loopback.git
cd Loopback
npm ci
npm run build
npm run demo
